extracted.intended_audience: PR agencies, consultancies and entrants preparing submissions for the Cannes Lions PR (PR Lions) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and judging rubric for preparing and submitting PR Lions entries, including category definitions, entry/eligibility rules, required materials, technical specs, jury scoring weights and the required written/case film components with word/time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of PR (for Cannes Lions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of PR for the purpose of Cannes Lions is the creative use of reputation management by the building and preservation of trust and understanding between individuals, businesses or organisations and their publics/audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR Lions are awarded to the freshest creative PR campaigns, programs and tactics that actively engage consumers/audiences to products/brands/organisations and demonstrate the highest levels of strategic planning, creativity and business results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission frequency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The same entry can only be entered a maximum of 3 times into PR Lions, if eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may be submitted up to 3 times across categories; entrants should ensure duplicate entries are appropriate to each category and tailor presentations to highlight category-relevant elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: A01. Food & Nutrition (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meats, fish, seafood, soups, delicatessen, fruits & vegetables, rice, pasta, pizza, sauces, mayonnaise, vinegar, oils, spices, herbs, pre-cooked & prepared meals, baby foods & baby milk, cream, butter, cheese, eggs, milk, margarine & spreads, chocolate, candy, chewing gum, potato crisps, snacks, nuts & dried fruit, sweet & savoury bars, cakes, biscuits, crackers, sugar, jam, honey, peanut butter, syrup, bread, crispbread, flour, baking ingredients, breakfast cereals, yoghurt & yoghurt drinks, desserts, ice cream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this sector when the PR campaign is for products/services listed; the same entry may only be submitted once in the Sectors section.

rubrics_metrics.name: A02. Automotive & Transport (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cars, Jeeps and 4-wheel drives, pick-up trucks, vans, lorries, motorbikes, tyres, auto products and services, spare parts, accessories incl. in-car hi-fi, petrol stations, petrol, oil, breakdown & servicing companies, car dealerships, car finance & leasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: A03. Healthcare & Wellbeing (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private healthcare & clinics, optical, medical & dental services, OTC drugs, psychiatrists and therapists, plastic surgeons etc., contact lenses, hearing aids, vitamins & herbal remedies, alternative therapies & medicines, diet supplements & products, pharmaceutical companies and providers and manufacturers of healthcare equipment e.g. hospital & dental equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: A04. Luxury Goods, Fashion & Beauty (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Luxury goods, fashion items, beauty products and related accessories (detailed list in guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes products associated with status/desirability and fashion/beauty product categories; refer to list for inclusions like perfumes, haircare, toothpaste, razors, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: A05. Other Consumer Products (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer products not covered by previous Food, Automotive, Healthcare, Luxury categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: A06. Media, Arts & Entertainment (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers, magazines, books, publishers, TV and radio stations, networks and programmes; theatre, cinema, museums, galleries, festivals, orchestras, nightclubs, bars etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: A07. Travel, Tourism & Leisure (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transport, airlines, train & bus companies, ferry & cruise lines, travel agencies, tourist boards, hotels, resorts, leisure & theme parks, gyms, health & diet clubs, sports.

rubrics_metrics.name: A08. Retail & Restaurants (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Home shopping, restaurants, fast food, department & specialist stores, supermarkets, DIY stores, drugstores, opticians, hairdressers, beauty salons, laundry, estate agents, photo-processors, TV/video rental, mail-order companies, auctions, e-commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: A09. Financial Services (incl. Investor Relations and Corporate Finance) (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks, credit cards, mortgages & loans, investment companies, insurance, pensions & REITs, mergers and acquisitions, privatizations, financial services marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: A10. Technology & Manufacturing (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology & telecoms services, mobile phones/apps, internet/service providers, video games, AV equipment, computer hardware/software; utilities, mining, aerospace, chemicals, plastics.

rubrics_metrics.name: A11. Charity & Not for Profit (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs and policies conducted on behalf of charities and/or not for Profit Organisations (anti-smoking, health, Aids awareness, blood & organ donation, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: A12. Public Sector (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs and policies conducted on behalf of public bodies (local authorities, councils, government departments or government authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: B01. Corporate Reputation & Communication (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns to build the image/increase the profile/shape the perceptions of a corporate brand, organization, trade associations, institutes and councils.

rubrics_metrics.name: B02. Public Affairs & Lobbying (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns planned to influence or inform the public policy agenda using lobbying or wider public affairs strategies; includes political or ballot initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: B03. Crisis Communications & Issue Management (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns to plan/handle the consequences of a crisis or an issue that may affect a company’s credibility and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: B04. Corporate Responsibility (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporations addressing social and ethical issues. (Note: environmental issues should be entered in B05).

rubrics_metrics.name: B05. Environmental (incl. Sustainability) (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns designed to address a green or environmental issue to protect or improve an organisation, product or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: B06. Internal Communications (incl. Employee Engagement) (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Business-to-employee communications and engagement, including change management.

rubrics_metrics.name: B07. Media Relations (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns designed to create/promote a positive profile of a product or service through mass media to change attitudes among targeted media audiences and meet client/project objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: B08. Events & Experiential (incl. stunts) (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns that use an event or stunt (trade show, conference, product launch, awards ceremony, field marketing, etc.) as part of a wider PR strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: B09. Celebrity Endorsement (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns that associate a celebrity with a product/service to reach awareness/business goals and build trust/affinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: B10. Sponsorship (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns that utilise sponsorship and/or partnership programs to support a product/service and meet awareness/business goals and enhance image.

rubrics_metrics.name: B11. Launch or Re-launch (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns created to launch or re-launch a product or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: B12. Brand Voice (incl. strategic storytelling) (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Customised PR strategy designed to guide a brand/organisation to communicate its point of view consistently and build emotional connection with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: B13. Research, Data Analytics & Insight Generation (practice/specialism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research, data or actionable insight that provides meaningful contribution to a PR program. Entrants should provide evidence of research/insight, quality of thinking and strategy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: C01. Use of Digital Platforms (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of websites, microsites, search engines, mobile, instant messaging, email marketing, digital POS, virtual worlds, downloadable apps and other digital PR techniques to execute or support a PR campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: C02. Community Building/Management (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social activity designed to engage, build or maintain a branded community or social-network-based community; judges consider passive vs active fans, engagement levels and appropriateness of communication to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: C03. Audience Targeting/Engagement (incl. social listening) (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of social channels/activities that rely on listening/responding strategies (audience surveys and monitoring). Demonstrated use of insights in communications initiatives will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: C04. Influencer Communications (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social initiatives/projects that feature a celebrity, social ambassadors or influencer (blogger, vlogger, etc.) to engage with an audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: C05. Response/Real-Time Activity (incl. crowdsourcing) (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted or nontargeted social activity that uses platforms to respond to world events, crises or other activity in a meaningful/creative way that may prompt social sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: C06. Use of Co-Creation & User Generated Content (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social activity designed to engage a community and encourage them to contribute or collaborate with a brand/organisation initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: C07. Innovative Use of Social or Community (digital & social category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative utilisation of existing or emerging social platforms and/or social activity. Evidence of innovation, engagement levels, social reach and strategy will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: D01. Multi-Markets Campaigns (geographies)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR campaigns implemented across multiple countries/markets. Entrants should detail implementation and results in different countries/markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: D02. Territory Marketing & Communication (incl. city/region/country branding) (geographies)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR programs/tactics designed to build/increase/promote the profile or image of a city/region/country.

rubrics_metrics.name: E01. Integrated Campaign led by PR (campaign type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns with multiple elements or channels that are predominantly PR driven. Entrants judged on how successfully chosen elements/channels are integrated and complement each other to communicate the brand’s message and/or change consumer awareness and attitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrated campaigns LED BY PR (except in exceptional circumstances) cannot be entered into Integrated Campaign LED BY Direct, Promo and Outdoor categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: E02. Costs/Creative Performance PR Campaign (campaign type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should demonstrate how well a low budget campaign (excluding all Agency fees) met its objectives. Entrants must detail total budget and information about PR tactics/initiatives used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low budget definitions vary by country; provide budget details (numbers, cost and volume) to justify category eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria: Strategy & Research (weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy and Research — allocated 30% of the jury vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges assess the quality of strategy and the research underpinning the campaign; evidence of insight, targeting and strategic planning is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria: Execution (weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Execution — allocated 20% of the jury vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges evaluate how effectively the strategy was implemented, the quality of execution and use of tactics/channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria: Creativity & Originality (weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity & Originality — allocated 20% of the jury vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges assess the originality and creative idea; fresh thinking and innovative approaches are rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria: Documented Results (weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented Results — allocated 30% of the jury vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must supply tangible and quantifiable results, measured against original objectives, demonstrating communication and business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlisting & voting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The shortlist is decided by a first round of voting. A computerised voting system selects the highest marks given in each category to form the shortlist. A grand Prix is selected from gold winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At all voting stages, a judge’s vote will not be counted for any entry submitted by his/her own company(ies) in his/her own country; votes may be removed for judges with regional/global roles. Jury decisions are final and binding; awards credit and trophies are given to the entrant company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and impartiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge’s vote will not be counted for any entry submitted by his or her own company(ies) in his or her own country; votes may be removed for judges with regional or global roles accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure impartiality; understand that jury composition and voting is independently audited (e.g., by PWC for 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: one campaign = one entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Each campaign constitutes one entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries relating to more than one campaign must be entered individually and paid for as separate entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: entries must relate to one campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries must relate to one campaign. Entries relating to more than one campaign (even if promoting the same client/product) must be entered individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: same entry in multiple PR categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The same entry may be submitted in up to 3 different PR categories, if eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure duplicates are appropriate to categories; tailor/adapt presentation for each category to highlight relevant elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: integrated campaign media leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: By definition, a campaign cannot be LED by more than one type of media. Integrated Campaigns LED BY PR cannot be entered into Integrated Campaign LED BY Outdoor, Direct and Promo & Activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: credits accuracy and immutability during judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Please carefully check and re-check the credits you have entered. If shortlisted or a winner, these credits will be published exactly as typed. Credits cannot be altered before and/or during judging; a specific post-festival period allows amendments (after which admin costs may apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect credits will be published as submitted; entrants should ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: explain/translate local references
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be in your own interest to explain or translate any specific word play or local, social, cultural or political references and nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clarification so an international jury can appreciate nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: confidential jury-only material option
rubrics_metrics.description: You will be offered the opportunity, when entering online, to submit information separately that will be kept confidential and submitted only to the jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confidential field for details that cannot be publicly published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rule: anonymity — no agency branding
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of impartiality, do not refer to the name of your agency or any contributing creative companies anywhere on your submission materials (copy, image/video/URL) with the exception of self-promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No agency branding or names should appear in presentation image, case film or written submission; this applies visually and verbally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material rule: no replacement media / upload final version
rubrics_metrics.description: WE WILL NOT ACCEPT REPLACEMENT MEDIA, so make sure the version uploaded is final and can be used for judging AND shown publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload 'holding media' (incorrect/fake JPG, MP3, MOV, MP4). Uploaded media may be used for festival screenings, website and public domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory material: Presentation Image (digital only)
rubrics_metrics.description: One digital Presentation Image in JPG format, 300 dpi, CMYK and A2 in size; uploaded online (5–15Mb). The presentation image must summarise the entry and be contained on one image; no more than 100 words in total on the presentation image (excluding words contained in visuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation should contain key visuals and a simple, clear summary in English of the written part. Do not include agency branding; adapt image to the PR category; ensure rights to use images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation Image content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation image should focus on key visuals and only key points of explanation; no more than 100 words; separate text into 3 clear sections such as Brief / Solution / Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple language, limit technical jargon/statistics, name image with the title of the entry, and ensure image meets technical specs (JPG, CMYK, 300 dpi, A2, 5–15Mb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials: what to supply (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply relevant support material depending on entry type; use barcoded labels for identification. Supporting materials might include planning documents, press releases, press clippings, online content, TV coverage, measurement/evaluation and research documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place materials within a letter-sized or A4 hardcover binder with no identifying marks (no entrant/agency names). Limit support material to most important pieces and supply only one copy of each piece. Physical materials become property of the Organisers and cannot be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials: media-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For live events/stunts/celebrity endorsement supply photographs. For digital/social categories supply URLs or original social accounts (with username/password if necessary). Broadcast material must be supplied as MOV/MP4 or MP3 for radio (with English transcript if not in case film).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display materials: send actual packaging/sample if reasonably sized or images if impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials format: images/photos/press clippings
rubrics_metrics.description: Images/Photos/Press clippings must be JPGs, 300 dpi, CMYK. Hard copy originals/proofs/photos may be supplied but should not be larger than 64 x 48 cm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials format: broadcast/video/audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcast materials, clips and videos: MOV/MP4 (uploaded online). Radio/audio files: MP3, bit rate 128 kbps, compression ratio 15:1, file size should not exceed 3Mb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload TV or cinema ads as support material if they are also contained within your case film. Websites/online materials must be submitted via a URL; make sure content is unbranded if posted for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Film: recommendation and compulsory tech requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are strongly recommended to prepare a case film. Upload the case film as MOV/MP4 via the online facility; file size should be no bigger than 350MB. No agency branding or contributing creatives/people must be visible on the case film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case film will be used for Jury deliberations and potentially in festival/public promotions; ensure it contains key visuals and clear English commentary; avoid showing creatives explaining the campaign to camera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Film: required two versions and lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply two versions: Long version — 2 minutes long (viewed by Jury and used for festival), and Short version — 30–45 seconds (shown at awards ceremony if entry wins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both should contain key visuals and simple clear English commentary summarising the written submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Film: encoding standards and technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended format MOV/H.264 or MP4/H.264. Preferred video aspect 4:3 or 16:9. Resolutions listed (e.g., 1280x720 HD 720p recommended). Audio: AAC Stereo 48kHz. Do not send Case Film on a URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow listed container/codec and resolution options; ensure audio encoded as AAC Stereo 48kHz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send case film as URL
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT send your Case Film on a URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload directly via the online upload facility; the jury will view the uploaded file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not upload 'holding media'
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not upload ‘holding media’ (i.e. incorrect/fake JPG, MP3, MOV, MP4, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uploaded media must be final and usable for judging and public display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials upload limits and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital images must be uploaded via the website (5–15Mb). Please name your image with the title of the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case film public-use consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Case Film long version may be used if your entry is a winner in post-Festival promotions and will be shown at the Festival for delegates to study entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the presentation concise and to the point; aim to grab attention quickly and use coherent voiceover with clear self-explanatory visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation image anonymity and adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no agency branding anywhere on your entry (with the exception of self-promotion) nor any reference to anyone who has contributed to the entry. You MUST adjust your presentation image to the category and section you are entering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If same entry is entered into other sections, adapt image for PR Lions specifically; entrants are responsible for ensuring rights to use images uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR Gold (visual/text template guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended characteristics of a PR gold winner presentation image/case: No Agency logo or branding; clear and concise text – 100 words maximum; key points from the written submission; minimal technical jargon and statistics; text presented in 3 clear sections; clear, relevant images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple language, be specific and to the point; no reference to agency or anyone involved in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Film creative guidance (do's and don'ts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to grab the attention of the jury as quickly as possible and go into more detail later. A coherent voiceover is often effective. Avoid showing creatives explaining the campaign to camera. You MUST NOT refer to any agency or individual who has contributed to the campaign, either visually or verbally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep case film concise, use clear visuals and voiceover; follow technical/format rules and file size limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Material delivery address and labelling (physical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivery address provided for physical support material. Label support material with the Reference Number clearly visible (use barcoded package label in PDF confirmation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting material sent becomes property of the Organisers and cannot be returned; use provided barcode labels to identify entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials binder requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Place supporting materials within a binder (letter-sized or A4), hardcover. The exterior and interior of the binder should have no type, images or identifying marks (this includes entrant and PR agency name and/or employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to the client name is acceptable. Limit supporting material to most important and relevant pieces and supply only one copy of each piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry written submission required — sample entry form structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the entry form you are required to provide a written submission; sample entry form contains structured sections and word counts (Entry Synopsis and detailed subsections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sample entry form for content and word limits; provide clear points that illustrate why the entry is PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry Synopsis: summary of the Campaign (250 words max)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of the Campaign (250 words max): brief overview from start to finish, including the challenge, objectives, strategy and execution and outcome. Must outline why the entry is appropriate to PR Lions and provide clear points illustrating key ‘PR’ elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise; ensure summary aligns with supporting materials and case film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: The Situation (100 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the organisation, business or individual for which the campaign was devised; describe the situation, problem or opportunity that elicited the need for the PR campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to word limit and succinctly describe context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: The Goal (100 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the goals and objectives of the campaign and the research that was undertaken to achieve the goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State measurable objectives where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: Strategy & Targeting (150 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strategy and planning for the campaign as well as the target audience and their relationship with the product/service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain strategic rationale, segmentation and targeting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: Execution (150 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe step by step how the plan was implemented including where, when and for how long. Note specific tools or tactics and whether the campaign ran as planned or was adapted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail implementation and tactical use; be concise and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: Documented Results (150 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include tangible and quantifiable results and show how they can be measured against the original objectives and achieved communication and business goals. All PR Lions entries are required to demonstrate at least two tiers of evaluation/results reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence across tiers such as output/awareness, knowledge/consideration, and action/business impact; use surveys, impressions, sales, social metrics, NPS changes, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required tiers of evaluation/results reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must demonstrate at least two tiers of evaluation/results reporting: output/awareness; knowledge/consideration; action/business impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: output/awareness — change in consumer awareness and attitude (survey), impressions, article counts, content views. Knowledge/Consideration — key message penetration, prominence, ratio favourable/unfavourable mentions, changes in NPS/purchase intent. Action/Business Impact — sales, donations, joining, increases in followers, shares, click-through rates, site traffic, time on site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: Results for category E02 only (150 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget information: entries in E02 should demonstrate how well a low budget campaign (excluding all agency fees) met its objectives. Provide information on budget details (numbers, cost and volume) to show the jury why the entry fits the category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about costs and show performance relative to spend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry section: Confidential Information (100 words max)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have confidential information that cannot be viewed by the general public, provide it here. This information will be reserved for the jury only and will not be published anywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section for sensitive data; jury-only field available on online entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry composition/metadata fields to supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of PR, Date of 1st Implementation, Placement (if relevant), ENTRY URL, Upload Media (Presentation Image compulsory, case film recommended, supporting images up to five, supporting content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure media uploaded can be used for both judging and public use; no replacements allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploadable media checklist and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital Presentation Image compulsory (JPG, 300 dpi, CMYK); Case Film highly recommended (2 minutes max, MP4 or MOV, ≤350MB); Short version 30–45 sec; Supporting images up to five (JPG, 300 dpi, CMYK); Supporting content including radio clips, TVCs, other documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to formats, sizes and the rule that uploaded media must be final.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: Eligibility window guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: My PR campaign has been running for 3 years, is it still eligible? Yes, as long as you have never entered the same campaign into PR Lions in previous years and you focus on the elements of the campaign that have run within March 2014 and the end of April 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must focus on elements implemented within the eligibility dates specified for the awards year.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: Category selection guidance (B04 vs B05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work created to address social or ethical issues must be entered into B04 Corporate Responsibility. Work created to address environmental issues including sustainability must be entered into B05 Environmental PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the category matching the primary purpose of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: Data required for Research, Analytics & Insight entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all relevant documentation surrounding the data and its creative use and implementation in your campaign (e.g., research documents, measurement and evaluation documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of research rigour, data sources, methodology and how insight informed strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: Labelling and sending support material
rubrics_metrics.description: Label the support material with the Reference Number clearly visible (e.g., PRL/001). Use the barcoded Package Label found in the PDF confirmation document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow packaging and labelling instructions to ensure supporting materials are correctly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: How long is my case film supposed to be?
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum of 2 minutes for the long case film version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide the short 30–45 second version for awards ceremony use.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ: Low budget category clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: How low does my budget need to be for E02: Costs/Creative Performance PR Campaign? Low budget campaigns differ from country to country. Provide budget details (numbers, cost and volume) to show the jury why the entry should be considered in this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply transparent budget documentation to justify classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Entry Form: Credits and client contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide credits for people with significant input and add additional company credits; provide a company contact (person involved in campaign) and a client contact (agency contact is not acceptable) for verification during judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List names in order of importance; client contact may be contacted to verify details/results.
